ai.description: *Minervarya krishnan* is a small frog (22–25 mm) with a brown dorsum featuring distinct longitudinal skin folds. It is distinguished by a dark interorbital bar and a pale, unspotted white throat.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Minervarya krishnan* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous, and prominent glandular fold along the dorsolateral region, which is absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: *Minervarya krishnan* inhabits moist deciduous forests and riparian zones in the Western Ghats, typically found near streams at mid-to-high elevations above 800 meters.
ai.behavior: The Minervarya krishnan is primarily nocturnal, emerging after dark to forage for small insects among leaf litter and damp vegetation near water bodies.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Minervarya krishnan* is an oviparous frog that breeds during the monsoon season, laying small clutches of eggs in shallow, temporary water bodies.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Minervarya krishnan* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, specifically inhabiting the high-altitude montane grasslands of Kerala and Tamil Nadu above 1,800 meters.
ai.callDescription: The call of *Minervarya krishnan* is a high-pitched, rhythmic, insect-like trill heard primarily from shallow, temporary rain pools and marshy grasslands during the monsoon.
